take_homes: Most of what we know sits in heads and corridors. Getting it written down so an agent can use it is a people and culture job, and that is the question I take to the leadership team.
Start agents as proposal-only: they draft and a person decides. That is also how I can explain it to the works council.
Judge any agent answer by whether it cites our own files. If it doesn't, it is generic and not ours.

monday.move: Write a one-page memory of my role-design and onboarding question with non-sensitive sources only. Then draft a proposal-only risk-scan agent on it and show it to one HR partner.
monday.who: Me, then one HR business partner
monday.when: Monday morning for the draft, Wednesday for the show-and-tell
monday.stop_condition: If any source contains employee data, I stop until the DPO and works council have been asked.
monday.blocker: Employee data needs the DPO and works council. I also am not sure my work laptop allows the desktop scheduler.

misconception.why: The module is about knowledge, not headcount. It suggests the scarce thing is written-down know-how and people who steer and judge, which makes 'which roles go' too narrow. It did not say that no roles go, so I am only shaken.

one_line: Useful idea that an AI is only as good as the knowledge we write down, but it is long on tool steps and says little about what it means for people.
